title: Building a Better Plate: The Simple Science of Balanced Eating
title_zh: 打造更好的餐盘：均衡饮食的简单科学
intro_zh: 本文约920词，包含6个CET-4核心词汇。通过餐盘法讲解健康饮食小常识，配有中文翻译和阅读理解题。

paragraphs.en: Many people feel confused about healthy eating. Diet trends change every year, and the same food is called good one day and bad the next. But nutrition scientists agree on a basic truth: a balanced meal is the foundation of good health. You do not need expensive ingredients or complicated recipes. In fact, the easiest way to improve your diet is to look at your own dinner plate. According to the World Health Organization, unhealthy diets are a major cause of chronic diseases such as heart disease and diabetes. This article will show you a practical method that is easy to remember and even easier to follow.
paragraphs.zh: 许多人对健康饮食感到困惑。饮食潮流每年都在变，同一种食物今天被说成好，明天又被说成坏。但营养科学家在一个基本事实上达成共识：均衡的膳食是健康的基础。你不需要昂贵的食材或复杂的食谱。事实上，改善饮食最简单的方法就是看看自己餐盘里的食物。据世界卫生组织称，不健康的饮食是心脏病和糖尿病等慢性疾病的主要原因。这篇文章将向你介绍一种实用方法，它既容易记住，也更容易执行。

paragraphs.en: Health experts from different countries recommend a simple tool called the Plate Method. The idea is to fill your plate in three parts: half with vegetables and fruits, one quarter with protein, and one quarter with whole grains. This method gives you a visual guide for every meal. You do not have to count calories or weigh food. Just use a normal plate and follow the proportions. The Plate Method works because it automatically limits the amount of less healthy food. It is used in schools, hospitals, and nutrition education programs around the world. Even a dinner plate with a 10-inch diameter can be a powerful health tool.
paragraphs.zh: 不同国家的健康专家推荐一种叫做“餐盘法”的简单工具。其理念是把你的餐盘分成三部分：一半是蔬菜水果，四分之一是蛋白质，四分之一是全谷物。这个方法为你每顿饭提供了一个视觉指南。你不必计算卡路里或称量食物。只需用一个普通餐盘并遵循比例即可。餐盘法之所以有效，是因为它自动限制了不太健康食物的量。它被世界各地的学校、医院和营养教育项目所使用。一个直径10英寸的餐盘也能成为强大的健康工具。

paragraphs.en: The largest section of your plate belongs to vegetables and fruits. These foods are rich in vitamins, minerals, and fiber. Different colors provide different nutrients. For example, dark leafy greens offer vitamin K, orange carrots and sweet potatoes supply beta-carotene, and red tomatoes provide lycopene. Blueberries and purple cabbage contain antioxidants that protect your cells. Try to include at least three colors at each meal. By doing so, you will naturally eat a wide range of helpful plant compounds. The UK's National Health Service recommends at least five portions of fruits and vegetables a day, which is often called '5-a-day'. Many people fall short of this goal.
paragraphs.zh: 餐盘最大的部分属于蔬菜和水果。这些食物富含维生素、矿物质和纤维。不同的颜色提供不同的营养物质。例如，深色绿叶菜提供维生素K，橙色胡萝卜和红薯提供β-胡萝卜素，红番茄提供番茄红素。蓝莓和紫甘蓝含有保护细胞的抗氧化剂。每餐尽量包含至少三种颜色。这样一来，你自然会摄入多种有益的植物化合物。英国国家医疗服务体系建议每天至少摄入五份蔬菜水果，这通常被称为“每日五份”。很多人都没有达到这个目标。

paragraphs.en: The second quarter of your plate is for protein. Protein repairs body tissues, builds muscle, and keeps you full. Good sources include fish, chicken, eggs, beans, lentils, tofu, and nuts. To get a complete set of amino acids, consume a mix of animal and plant proteins. For example, a meal with beans and rice provides complete protein. A simple guide for a portion of meat is the size of your palm, about 85 grams. For beans or yogurt, one cup is a typical serving. Do not make the protein section too large; your body only needs this amount at each meal. Fish like salmon and sardines are rich in omega-3 fatty acids, which are good for the brain.
paragraphs.zh: 餐盘的第二块区域留给蛋白质。蛋白质修复身体组织、构建肌肉并产生饱腹感。好的来源包括鱼、鸡肉、鸡蛋、豆类、扁豆、豆腐和坚果。为了获得完整的氨基酸组合，摄入动物和植物蛋白质的混合搭配。例如，豆类和米饭搭配就能提供完全蛋白质。一个简单的肉类份量指南是手掌大小，约85克。对于豆类或酸奶，一杯是典型份量。不要将蛋白质部分做得太大；你的身体每餐只需要这些量。三文鱼和沙丁鱼等鱼类富含对大脑有益的omega-3脂肪酸。

paragraphs.en: The remaining quarter of your plate should be whole grains. Brown rice, oats, quinoa, whole-wheat bread, and barley are excellent choices. They provide fiber, B vitamins, and complex carbohydrates that give you steady energy. Unlike refined grains, whole grains are digested slowly, so you feel satisfied for hours. Choosing whole grains over white bread or white rice can lower blood sugar spikes and reduce the risk of heart disease. This small daily choice is beneficial for your long-term health. A high-fiber diet can also reduce the risk of constipation and bowel disease. Even replacing one serving of refined grains a day makes a measurable difference.
paragraphs.zh: 餐盘剩下的四分之一应为全谷物。糙米、燕麦、藜麦、全麦面包和大麦都是很好的选择。它们提供纤维、B族维生素和复合碳水化合物，为你带来稳定的能量。与精制谷物不同，全谷物消化缓慢，所以你能保持数小时的饱腹感。选择全谷物而非白面包或白米饭，可以降低血糖飙升的风险，并减少心脏病的发生几率。这个小小的日常选择对你的长期健康有益。高纤维饮食还能降低便秘和肠道疾病的风险。即使每天只把一份精制谷物换成全谷物，也能产生可衡量的效果。

paragraphs.en: Now let's talk about processed foods. These are foods that have been changed from their natural state, such as packaged snacks, sugary drinks, chips, and fast food. They often contain high amounts of added sugar, salt, and unhealthy trans fats. Eating too much of them is linked to obesity, diabetes, and heart disease. It is important to read nutrition labels. Pay attention to the serving size. The label may say one serving has 150 calories, but the whole bag may contain three servings. If you eat the whole bag, you are actually consuming 450 calories. This is why controlling your portion is critical. Common added sugars go by many names, such as high-fructose corn syrup, cane sugar, and maltose.
paragraphs.zh: 现在我们来谈谈加工食品。这些食品在自然状态上发生了改变，比如包装零食、含糖饮料、薯片和快餐。它们通常含有大量添加糖、盐和不健康的反式脂肪。摄入过多与肥胖、糖尿病和心脏病有关。阅读营养标签很重要。注意份量大小。标签可能说一份含150卡路里，但整袋可能含有三份。如果你吃掉整袋，实际上摄入了450卡路里。这就是为什么控制份量至关重要。常见的添加糖有许多名称，如高果糖玉米糖浆、蔗糖和麦芽糖。

paragraphs.en: Water is another key part of healthy eating. Your body needs water to digest food, transport nutrients, and remove waste. Experts often recommend drinking about eight glasses of water a day, but this can vary depending on your activity level and climate. Not all drinks are equal. Sugary sodas and fruit juices add extra calories without making you feel full. Instead, choose water, unsweetened tea, or coffee in moderate amounts. Even mild dehydration can cause headaches, tiredness, and poor concentration. Also, eating a variety of foods, including fruits and vegetables with high water content, helps you stay hydrated.
paragraphs.zh: 水是健康饮食的另一个关键部分。你的身体需要水来消化食物、输送营养物质和排除废物。专家通常建议每天喝大约八杯水，但这取决于你的活动水平和气候。并非所有饮料都一样。含糖汽水和果汁会增加额外卡路里却带不来饱腹感。相反，选择白开水、无糖茶或适量咖啡。即使轻度脱水也会导致头痛、疲劳和注意力不集中。此外，吃多种多样食物，包括含水量高的蔬果，有助于保持水分。

paragraphs.en: Remember, you do not have to change everything overnight. Small steps lead to lasting habits. Start by filling half of your dinner plate with vegetables and fruits, then gradually replace white rice with whole grains, and try one new plant protein each week. Pay attention to hunger cues and eat slowly. Enjoying your food is part of healthy eating. Planning meals ahead can also help you stay on track. A balanced plate is not about perfection; it is about making better choices most of the time. Your future self will thank you.
paragraphs.zh: 记住，你不需要一夜之间改变一切。小步骤能带来持久的习惯。从晚餐盘里装上一半蔬菜水果开始，然后逐渐用全谷物代替白米饭，每周尝试一种新的植物蛋白。注意饥饿信号，慢慢进食。享受食物是健康饮食的一部分。提前计划餐食也能帮助你保持正轨。均衡的餐盘不是追求完美，而是在大多数时候做出更好的选择。未来的你会感谢现在的你。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A simple plate-based method can help you eat healthily.
Fruits and vegetables are more expensive than meat.
Drinking water is the only way to stay healthy.
Processed foods should be eaten with every meal.
questions.explain: 文章介绍餐盘法，用盘子的一半蔬菜水果、四分之一蛋白质、四分之一全谷物的方法来指导均衡饮食，故选A。B、C、D均不是文章主旨。

questions.q: According to the Plate Method, what should fill half of your plate?
questions.explain: 文章第二段明确提到“half with vegetables and fruits”，即一半是蔬菜和水果，故选B。

questions.q: What can be inferred from the example about the bag of chips?
options: The bag contains exactly one serving.
People often misjudge how many calories they eat from packaged snacks.
Labels show the correct calories for the whole package.
questions.explain: 例子说标签上一份是150卡路里，但整袋含三份，如果吃掉整袋就摄入450卡路里，说明人们常忽略份量而多摄入热量，故选B。A与事实相反，C与原文不符，D错误。

questions.q: In the passage, the word 'portion' is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 文中“portion”指“一份食物”，与serving同义，故选C。A烹饪方法，B营养类型，D食品标签均不对。
